findings.title: Async legacy Create uses pre-creation input object instead of created object
findings.body: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, `d.Storage.Create` returns `created`, which contains server-generated fields such as `Name` (when `GenerateName` is used), `UID`, and `ResourceVersion`. However, the async goroutine calls `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` with the original `obj` rather than `created` (or a deep copy of `created`). When `GenerateName` is used, `obj` has no name or a different UID than what was persisted in unified storage, causing the legacy store to either fail or create an inconsistent resource with a different identifier. Furthermore, passing `obj` or `created` without deep-copying into a background goroutine risks data races while the main goroutine serializes `created` for the response.

findings.title: Async legacy writes use the request context, which is canceled when the HTTP handler returns
findings.body: In `Create` (line 51), `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163), the background goroutines derive their timeout context directly from the request `ctx` (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). Because the goroutines run asynchronously and the methods return immediately after unified storage completes, the HTTP server will finish the request and cancel `ctx` while the legacy storage operation is still in flight, causing the background legacy writes to fail with `context.Canceled`. The context passed to the goroutine should be detached from parent cancellation (e.g. `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`).

findings.title: Incorrect metric recording methods and label values in Mode 3 operations
findings.body:
Multiple metric recording calls in `DualWriterMode3` record to the wrong metric or with the wrong label:
1. Line 45 (`Create`): When `d.Storage.Create` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
2. Line 106 (`Delete`): When `d.Storage.Delete` succeeds, `name` (the object instance name, which is also high-cardinality) is passed as the `kind` argument in `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` instead of `options.Kind`.
3. Line 129 (`Update`): When `d.Storage.Update` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
4. Line 166 (`DeleteCollection`): In the async goroutine for `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection`, `d.recordStorageDuration` is called instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`.

findings.title: Shared mock.Mock instance in unit tests causes data races with async legacy writes
findings.body: In `TestMode3_Create`, `TestMode3_Delete`, `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, and `TestMode3_Update`, both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` share the same `*mock.Mock` instance `m`, and the tests do not synchronize with the background goroutines spawned by `DualWriterMode3`. In `Delete` and `DeleteCollection`, no mock expectations are even registered for the legacy calls (`setupLegacyFn` is missing), so if the background goroutine runs before or during test completion, `testify/mock` will panic with an unexpected method call or trigger a data race on `m.Calls`.
